fichas.title: Insolation and Sun Paths
fichas.summary: Explains how to assess insolation on a planned building by overlaying its compass-oriented plan on sun-path diagrams. The diagrams show solar paths for the summer solstice and the spring and autumn equinoxes at 51.5° north. The text describes latitude adjustments, azimuth and local-time readings, possible and actual sunshine duration, and the seasonal delay between solar elevation and outdoor warmth.
uses: Assessing sunlight and insolation on a planned building
Interpreting sun-path diagrams for different seasons and latitudes
Estimating possible and actual sunshine duration

dimensions.label: Reference latitude
dimensions.context: Latitude used for the illustrated sun paths; London, Cardiff and Dortmund are given as examples.

dimensions.label: Southern-area latitude
dimensions.context: For the southern area, 3.5° is added to calculated solar elevations.
dimensions.ocr_raw: latitude 48° north (Freiburg im Breisgau – Munich – Salzburg – Vienna), 3.5° should be added to the calculated solar elevations.

dimensions.label: Solar-elevation adjustment for southern areas
dimensions.context: Added to calculated solar elevations for the stated southern area.
dimensions.ocr_raw: 3.5° should be added to the calculated solar elevations.

dimensions.label: Northern-area latitude
dimensions.context: For the northern area, 3.5° is deducted from calculated solar elevations.
dimensions.ocr_raw: latitude 55° north (Edinburgh – Newcastle – Bornholm – Königsberg), 3.5° should be deducted.

dimensions.label: Solar-elevation adjustment for northern areas
dimensions.context: Deducted for the stated northern area.

dimensions.label: Reference longitude
dimensions.context: Longitude used for the standard local times within Germany; identified as the Central European Time meridian.
dimensions.ocr_raw: locations at longitude 15° east (Görlitz – Stargard – Bornholm = meridian of Central European Time).

dimensions.label: Local-time adjustment per degree of longitude
dimensions.context: The local time is earlier east of 15° longitude and later west of it.
dimensions.ocr_raw: the local time is 4 minutes earlier than the standard time for every degree of longitude; for locations to the west of 15° = 4 minutes later than the standard time per degree.

dimensions.label: Greenwich longitude
dimensions.context: The text states that local time in Greenwich is 60 minutes later than standard time.
dimensions.ocr_raw: In London, specifically in Greenwich at 0° longitude, the local time is therefore 60 minutes later than the standard time.

dimensions.label: Greenwich local-time difference
dimensions.context: Local time in Greenwich is stated to be later than standard time.
dimensions.ocr_raw: the local time is therefore 60 minutes later than the standard time.

dimensions.label: Possible insolation duration, May to July
dimensions.context: Possible duration during the days from 21 May to 21 July; the printed range is retained in the OCR text.
dimensions.ocr_raw: The possible duration of insolation during the days from 21 May to 21 July = 1616% hours

dimensions.label: Actual insolation relative to possible duration
dimensions.context: The text says actual insolation is scarcely this proportion of the possible-duration figures because of clouds and mist.
dimensions.ocr_raw: The actual amount of insolation is scarcely 40% of the above figures on account of clouds and mist.

dimensions.label: Warmth-curve delay
dimensions.context: Approximate delay compared with the solar-elevation curve.
dimensions.ocr_raw: The warmth curve is delayed by about 1 month compared to the solar elevation curve

dimensions.label: Monthly change in insolation duration
dimensions.context: The text says duration changes by almost this amount per month between the stated seasonal ranges.
dimensions.ocr_raw: the duration of insolation changes by almost 2 hours per month.

dimensions.label: Berlin insolation in July
dimensions.context: Described as an almost value for Berlin in July.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Berlin has relatively favourable conditions (in July almost 50%, Stuttgart 35%).

dimensions.label: Stuttgart insolation
dimensions.context: Given as a comparative example of actual insolation conditions.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Berlin has relatively favourable conditions (in July almost 50%, Stuttgart 35%).
